_meta.description: Market and notified prices of fuels used in Indian industrial process heating -- coal, diesel, LPG, piped natural gas, and biomass variants -- for use by the Finance and Baseline Economics modules of the Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer.

FUEL_COAL.description: Domestic non-coking coal as used for industrial boilers/furnaces in Indian MSMEs. Coal India Ltd (CIL) notifies ex-mine prices by grade (G1 highest calorific value to G17 lowest); an independent delivered/landed-cost estimate is also tracked for MSME-scale procurement, since freight, handling, and dealer margins are not captured in the ex-mine price.

research.summary: CIL notified ex-mine price for G3 (high calorific value, non-coking) grade coal.
research.assumptions: Ex-mine gate price; excludes GST, royalty, freight, and handling.
research.limitations: Grade-wise notified prices are revised periodically by CIL; verify current notification before use in a live quote.

research.summary: CIL notified ex-mine price for G11 (mid calorific value, non-coking) grade coal, the grade most commonly supplied to small/medium industrial boilers.
research.assumptions: Ex-mine gate price; excludes GST, royalty, freight, and handling.
research.limitations: Regional and colliery-level variation within a grade is not captured.

research.summary: CIL notified ex-mine price for G13 (mid-low calorific value, non-coking) grade coal.
CIL notified ex-mine price for G15 (low calorific value, non-coking) grade coal.
Independent delivered/landed-cost estimate for industrial non-coking coal reaching a small/medium factory gate, i.e. inclusive of an assumed freight and handling margin.
research.assumptions: Assumes typical road-freight distance and dealer margin for MSME-scale lots (as opposed to bulk rail-linked large-industry procurement).
research.limitations: This figure is NOT reconcilable with the ex-mine grade prices above via a stated freight assumption -- treat as an independently sourced delivered-cost estimate, not (ex-mine price + known transport cost).

research.summary: Assumed annual escalation rate for coal price forecasting in payback/NPV calculations.
research.assumptions: Point estimate from a 5-7% per year plausible range, based on historical CIL notified-price revision trends.
research.limitations: Not a published CIL forecast; genuinely an internal planning assumption. Low confidence -- do not present as an official projection.

research.summary: Coal remains the dominant legacy industrial fuel for Indian MSMEs; CIL notified grade prices are the primary-source input, supplemented by a delivered-cost estimate.
research.assumptions: MSME procurement is assumed to occur through dealers/traders rather than direct CIL linkage, which explains the gap between ex-mine and delivered price bases.
research.limitations: State-level and seasonal price variation, and imported coal blending, are not modelled in this dataset.

FUEL_DIESEL_HSD.description: High-speed diesel (HSD) used for industrial thermal applications and backup generation.

research.summary: Retail reference price for industrial bulk diesel purchase.
research.assumptions: Retail pump-price reference; large-volume industrial buyers may negotiate a discount not captured here.
research.limitations: State-level VAT differences on diesel are significant in India and are not broken out in this single national reference figure.

FUEL_LPG.description: Liquefied petroleum gas used for direct-fired industrial heating, drying, and process applications.

research.summary: Retail/industrial reference price for bulk LPG supply.
research.assumptions: Commercial/industrial LPG rate, distinct from subsidized domestic-cylinder pricing.
research.limitations: Oil marketing company (OMC) commercial LPG prices are revised monthly; treat as indicative and re-verify against the current OMC price list before use.

FUEL_NATURAL_GAS_PNG.description: Piped natural gas (PNG) supplied to industrial consumers, typically via a city/geographic gas distribution (CGD) network.

research.summary: Retail reference price for industrial PNG supply.
research.assumptions: Single national reference; actual industrial PNG price is CGD-entity specific and depends on the underlying gas-source mix (APM, non-APM, spot RLNG).
research.limitations: No state/city-gas-distribution-entity breakdown is available in this dataset.

research.summary: Domestic APM gas is priced via a formula benchmarked to a basket of international hub prices (Henry Hub, Alberta, NBP, Russia), reformed on the Kirit Parikh Committee recommendations, with a price ceiling and floor.
research.limitations: No single INR/SCM value is published as a fixed number -- the formula output varies monthly with the international benchmark basket, so it is recorded as a policy/formula reference rather than a numeric price here.

FUEL_BIOMASS.description: Agricultural-residue and processed biomass fuels used as a coal-substitute in industrial boilers. Prices vary widely by feedstock, processing (loose vs. pelletized/briquetted), and region.

research.summary: Loose rice husk, a widely available boiler fuel in paddy-growing regions.
Loose wheat straw, seasonal availability concentrated post-harvest.
Wet (as-received) sugarcane bagasse, typically sourced near sugar mills.
research.limitations: Often captive to sugar mills for their own cogeneration; open-market availability to third-party MSMEs may be limited.

research.summary: Dried sugarcane bagasse, higher calorific value than wet bagasse.
Industrial wood chips from forestry/sawmill residue.
Densified biomass briquettes, higher cost than loose biomass but easier handling, storage, and combustion control.
General industrial biomass pellets (mixed feedstock).
Pelletized rice husk.
Pelletized paddy straw (parali), relevant to stubble-burning mitigation policy in north India.
research.limitations: Regionally concentrated supply (Punjab, Haryana, western UP); not a pan-India commodity price.

research.summary: Wood pellets, the highest-cost biomass variant tracked, reflecting processing and feedstock cost.
Assumed annual escalation rate for biomass price forecasting.
research.assumptions: Point estimate from a 4-6% per year plausible range.
research.limitations: Biomass co-firing mandates for thermal power plants create incremental demand pressure not fully reflected in a simple linear escalation assumption.

research.summary: Biomass prices are the least standardized in this dataset: no single regulator publishes an official biomass price index, so all figures are secondary-source compiled estimates rather than notified/regulated prices.
research.assumptions: Prices assume open-market third-party purchase, not captive/on-site residue.
research.limitations: Significant regional, seasonal, and quality (moisture content, calorific value) variation exists and is not captured by a single national price point per variant.

cross_references.note: Entity IDs referenced under related_entities are expected to exist in knowledge-base/technologies/, knowledge-base/emissions/, knowledge-base/industries/, and knowledge-base/finance/subsidies.json respectively; this file does not duplicate their data, only points to them by ID.
